Auburn University
United States · Mathematics PhD
Roster and rank verification handled separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A four-year accredited bachelor’s degree or equivalent is sufficient; a math/statistics bachelor’s is not strictly
required, but deficiencies may require extra coursework. A UChicago mathematics degree meets the
degree-type criterion, subject to academic selection. International applications are accepted. [s2] [s3] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply through Graduate School and separately complete mathematics GTA application if funding is wanted.
Attach the required mathematics-course page and arrange three references. Request confirmation of the
funding deadline and whether portal letters satisfy the GTA form. A completed US degree English exemption
requires official degree transcript and review. [s1] [s3] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance supervisor agreement stated. For GTA/PGRF logistics contact GPO yzc0009@auburn.edu. Brown,
Schenck and Oeding are direct algebraic-geometry fits; Huang in Lie theory; Leonard in
computational/function-field geometry. [s1] [s9] [s11]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate application permits save/return and tracks receipt. Referees receive question form plus optional letter
upload. Unofficial transcripts are reviewable; official records required before registration. GTA funding has a
separate form. [s2] [s5] [s6]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Central international page explicitly gives 2027-28 cost and new TOEFL scale. Mathematics page mixes
updated GRE optional policy with older mandatory-GRE and English text. Three months versus 90 days differ
by two days for Fall 2027. Admission transcript and GTA reference delivery instructions also need
reconciliation. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6] [s10]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application; Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Conflict]
Department accepts applications year-round, prefers fall for GTA positions, and publishes no exact
mathematics complete-file date. Central international rules say at least 90 days before classes, while
international page says three months. Fall 2027 classes begin August 16: calendar arithmetic yields May 18 for
90 days, May 16 for three months. Use May 16 at latest pending confirmation; these are derived administrative
limits, NOT funding priority dates. All relevant materials and applicable official scores must arrive. [s1] [s2] [s3]
[s10]

Funding consideration [Unresolved]
No exact 2027 GTA date is published; contact GPO Yanzhao Cao (yzc0009@auburn.edu) early. PGRF
nomination deadlines are set internally by college, described generally as early spring. Do not rely on the May
administrative deadline for funding. [s1] [s8] [s9]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Assistantship offer letter must state its own acceptance deadline. No universal 2027 date established by the
cited public sources. [s7]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Current central minimum: TOEFL after January 21, 2026 total 4.5 with each component ≥4; earlier TOEFL 79
with each ≥16; IELTS 6.5; Duolingo 115 with each ≥110. Self-report initially, then official scores immediately;
review does not proceed without official scores or approved exemption. [s3]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
Completed US accredited degree may receive exemption after official transcript showing degree award arrives;
central policy makes exemptions case-by-case. Department FAQ states US degrees waive TOEFL more
categorically. An in-progress UChicago degree is not expressly exempt: confirm before deciding to skip testing.
[s1] [s3] [s5]
GRE General [Conflict]
Recommended, not required: current application checklist and central Mathematics MS/PhD waiver list agree.
An older FAQ paragraph and GTA form still say all applicants need GRE; these are inconsistent with the
updated checklist. [s1] [s4] [s6]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required; department FAQ and GTA form explicitly say so. Optional submission preference is not further
classified. [s1] [s6]

sections.title: Academic records
sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Conflict]
All colleges/universities attended, including current study. Central permits unofficial transcript uploads for
review; official institution-issued transcripts are needed before registration. Department checklist instead says
official at application. Original-language documents plus certified English translations if applicable; US
transcripts can be sent securely to graduatetranscripts@auburn.edu. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
GTA application requires an attached page listing EVERY math class, undergraduate and graduate separately:
course name, institution, date taken and grade. No explicit font/word limit; attach a page to the form. It does
not request textbook titles or full descriptions. [s6]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
No separate course descriptions are requested in the GTA form or public admission checklist. [s1] [s6]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
GTA form explicitly requests three referees with names, addresses and positions and asks them to send letters
to the department. General admission portal displays the program-specific count; mathematics checklist itself
omits the number. Plan on three and ask whether the same Slate letters satisfy GTA consideration. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
PGRF requires a separate nomination letter from the proposed major professor or department chair, plus the

chair’s financial-support statement, nomination cover form and applicant CV. This is distinct from the three
external admission references. [s9]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Central application sends referees an email invitation after their details are provided, containing questions and
an optional typed/PDF letter upload. Exact trigger relative to saving details and submitting the application is
not explicit. GTA form’s direct-to-department instruction needs reconciliation. [s2] [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Slate status tracking shows receipt of recommendations and other materials. Unofficial transcript review can
proceed while official-transcript checklist still says awaiting. [s5]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
No published update/reuse or replacement rule was located in the application instructions or FAQ. [s2] [s5]

nomination packet, with no public length limit; nominating unit emails the full packet as one PDF. [s1] [s9]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Mathematics publishes monthly stipend depending on assigned teaching but no numeric annual rate.
Qualifying GTAs receive tuition waiver capped at 75 doctoral credits (38 master’s). Health insurance is
subsidized centrally, not described as fully paid. Request the actual stipend, paid months, fees and insurance
contribution. [s1] [s7]
Years of support [Unresolved]
Central assistantship guidance says teaching appointments are generally nine months and RAs twelve, with
exceptions. No math guarantee of five/six years found. Offer must state workload, length, stipend,
renewal/evaluation terms and acceptance deadline. [s7]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International GTAs are eligible but must demonstrate speaking proficiency independently of admission: current
TOEFL speaking 4.5 (23 old), IELTS speaking 7, Duolingo speaking 130 or Auburn iTEP speaking 4.5.
Department’s older iTEP 4.4/TSE instructions conflict with current central rule. Training/course may be
required. [s1] [s3]

Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Admission, enrollment, satisfactory progress and background check are required for assistantship
appointment; combined campus appointments max 0.50 FTE/20 hours weekly. International Statement of
Finances and certified evidence are required before admission letter/I-20 release; central estimate is $56,975
for 2027-28. Department warns GTA support may fall short of required financial sponsorship. [s1] [s3] [s7]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
YES: mathematics GTA form is mandatory for consideration; without it committee assumes no interest. Use the
working top-of-page TA-form link; the older FAQ PDF link redirects to department home. Confirm submission
method with GPO because paper form gives a postal return address and direct reference instructions. [s1] [s6]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
PGRF offers ≥$37,000 per year for three years ($15,000 Presidential + ≥$7,000 Dean’s + ≥$15,000 RA),
tuition waiver but excludes enrollment/student fees. Faculty/college nomination required; full-time study,
progress and professional development conditions. International-specific exclusion is not stated; confirm
eligibility. Departmental fellowships and occasional research grants also exist. [s1] [s8] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
$70 international, nonrefundable, payable by credit card; application is not processed until paid. Domestic fee
is $60. [s2] [s3]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Published categories: current Auburn graduate students, full-time Auburn employees, active-duty military with
confirming letter, or second application to approved dual program. Select qualifying exemption in portal
payment section and provide evidence. UChicago/F-1 alone is not a listed category. [s2] [s5]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
1. Algebraic geometry / commutative algebra
Michael K. Brown
Derived categories, toric varieties, sheaf cohomology, matrix factorizations and homological mirror symmetry.
[s11] [s12]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Tate resolutions on toric varieties
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
Henry (Hal) Schenck
Toric varieties, arrangements, syzygies, Gorenstein rings and computational geometry; applications to physics
and dynamics. [s11] [s14]

Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Algebraic aspects of homogeneous Kuramoto oscillators
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
2. Algebraic geometry / representation theory
Luke Oeding
Tensor geometry, invariant/representation theory, secant varieties and quantum information. [s11] [s13]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2025 · Tensor decompositions with applications to local unitary and stochastic local operations and
classical communication equivalence of multipartite pure states
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
3. Lie groups / algebraic groups
Huajun Huang
Matrix/Lie-group decompositions, algebraic-group actions and matrix means; recent work also in data science.
[s11] [s15]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2026 · Multiplicative trace and spectrum preservers on stochastic matrices
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.
4. Function fields / computational geometry
Douglas Leonard
Desingularization of function fields, integral closures, algebraic-geometric codes and algebraic combinatorics.
Official personal page latest dated 2019; recent activity and supervision need confirmation. [s11] [s16]
Listed on official departmental faculty pages; availability to supervise new PhD students is not published.
Research evidence: 2019 · Desingularization of function fields (paper listed as ArXiv 2019)
Recent research evidence; verify supervision availability separately.

Auburn University
United States · Mathematics PhD
Roster and rank verification handled separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Separate GTA application includes a mandatory math-course page and three references.
• Do not use the administrative May deadline as a funding deadline.
• English waiver before UChicago graduation is unresolved; teaching speaking certification is separate.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A four-year accredited bachelor’s degree or equivalent is sufficient; a math/statistics bachelor’s is not strictly
required, but deficiencies may require extra coursework. A UChicago mathematics degree meets the
degree-type criterion, subject to academic selection. International applications are accepted. [s2] [s3] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply through Graduate School and separately complete mathematics GTA application if funding is wanted.
Attach the required mathematics-course page and arrange three references. Request confirmation of the
funding deadline and whether portal letters satisfy the GTA form. A completed US degree English exemption
requires official degree transcript and review. [s1] [s3] [s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No advance supervisor agreement stated. For GTA/PGRF logistics contact GPO yzc0009@auburn.edu. Brown,
Schenck and Oeding are direct algebraic-geometry fits; Huang in Lie theory; Leonard in
computational/function-field geometry. [s1] [s9] [s11]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Slate application permits save/return and tracks receipt. Referees receive question form plus optional letter
upload. Unofficial transcripts are reviewable; official records required before registration. GTA funding has a
separate form. [s2] [s5] [s6]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Central international page explicitly gives 2027-28 cost and new TOEFL scale. Mathematics page mixes
updated GRE optional policy with older mandatory-GRE and English text. Three months versus 90 days differ
by two days for Fall 2027. Admission transcript and GTA reference delivery instructions also need
reconciliation. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6] [s10]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application; Reference receipt; Test-score receipt; Supporting documents [Conflict]
Department accepts applications year-round, prefers fall for GTA positions, and publishes no exact
mathematics complete-file date. Central international rules say at least 90 days before classes, while
international page says three months. Fall 2027 classes begin August 16: calendar arithmetic yields May 18 for
90 days, May 16 for three months. Use May 16 at latest pending confirmation; these are derived administrative
limits, NOT funding priority dates. All relevant materials and applicable official scores must arrive. [s1] [s2] [s3]
[s10]

Funding consideration [Unresolved]
No exact 2027 GTA date is published; contact GPO Yanzhao Cao (yzc0009@auburn.edu) early. PGRF
nomination deadlines are set internally by college, described generally as early spring. Do not rely on the May
administrative deadline for funding. [s1] [s8] [s9]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
Assistantship offer letter must state its own acceptance deadline. No universal 2027 date established by the
cited public sources. [s7]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
Current central minimum: TOEFL after January 21, 2026 total 4.5 with each component ≥4; earlier TOEFL 79
with each ≥16; IELTS 6.5; Duolingo 115 with each ≥110. Self-report initially, then official scores immediately;
review does not proceed without official scores or approved exemption. [s3]
UChicago English exemption [Conflict]
Completed US accredited degree may receive exemption after official transcript showing degree award arrives;
central policy makes exemptions case-by-case. Department FAQ states US degrees waive TOEFL more
categorically. An in-progress UChicago degree is not expressly exempt: confirm before deciding to skip testing.
[s1] [s3] [s5]
GRE General [Conflict]
Recommended, not required: current application checklist and central Mathematics MS/PhD waiver list agree.
An older FAQ paragraph and GTA form still say all applicants need GRE; these are inconsistent with the
updated checklist. [s1] [s4] [s6]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required; department FAQ and GTA form explicitly say so. Optional submission preference is not further
classified. [s1] [s6]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Conflict]
All colleges/universities attended, including current study. Central permits unofficial transcript uploads for
review; official institution-issued transcripts are needed before registration. Department checklist instead says
official at application. Original-language documents plus certified English translations if applicable; US
transcripts can be sent securely to graduatetranscripts@auburn.edu. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
GTA application requires an attached page listing EVERY math class, undergraduate and graduate separately:
course name, institution, date taken and grade. No explicit font/word limit; attach a page to the form. It does
not request textbook titles or full descriptions. [s6]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
No separate course descriptions are requested in the GTA form or public admission checklist. [s1] [s6]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
GTA form explicitly requests three referees with names, addresses and positions and asks them to send letters
to the department. General admission portal displays the program-specific count; mathematics checklist itself
omits the number. Plan on three and ask whether the same Slate letters satisfy GTA consideration. [s1] [s2] [s6]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
PGRF requires a separate nomination letter from the proposed major professor or department chair, plus the

chair’s financial-support statement, nomination cover form and applicant CV. This is distinct from the three
external admission references. [s9]
What sends the invitation; Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
Central application sends referees an email invitation after their details are provided, containing questions and
an optional typed/PDF letter upload. Exact trigger relative to saving details and submitting the application is
not explicit. GTA form’s direct-to-department instruction needs reconciliation. [s2] [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Slate status tracking shows receipt of recommendations and other materials. Unofficial transcript review can
proceed while official-transcript checklist still says awaiting. [s5]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
No published update/reuse or replacement rule was located in the application instructions or FAQ. [s2] [s5]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Not explicitly listed on mathematics admission checklist. A copy of CV/résumé IS required for a PGRF
nomination packet, with no public length limit; nominating unit emails the full packet as one PDF. [s1] [s9]
Statement of purpose; Personal / background statement; Research-interest statement; Research
proposal; Writing sample / thesis / research summary; Publications list [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
GTA application requires an attached page listing EVERY math class, undergraduate and graduate separately:
course name, institution, date taken and grade. No explicit font/word limit; attach a page to the form. It does
not request textbook titles or full descriptions. [s6]
Scholarship essays; Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Separate GTA form includes employment/education history, honors and activities, proposed field, GPAs,
language-reading ability, other significant information and a question requiring explanation if ever
discharged/forced to resign. No separate long essay limit is supplied. PGRF applicant materials include CV;
faculty supply nomination and support letters in one PDF packet. [s6] [s9]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Mathematics publishes monthly stipend depending on assigned teaching but no numeric annual rate.
Qualifying GTAs receive tuition waiver capped at 75 doctoral credits (38 master’s). Health insurance is
subsidized centrally, not described as fully paid. Request the actual stipend, paid months, fees and insurance
contribution. [s1] [s7]
Years of support [Unresolved]
Central assistantship guidance says teaching appointments are generally nine months and RAs twelve, with
exceptions. No math guarantee of five/six years found. Offer must state workload, length, stipend,
renewal/evaluation terms and acceptance deadline. [s7]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International GTAs are eligible but must demonstrate speaking proficiency independently of admission: current
TOEFL speaking 4.5 (23 old), IELTS speaking 7, Duolingo speaking 130 or Auburn iTEP speaking 4.5.
Department’s older iTEP 4.4/TSE instructions conflict with current central rule. Training/course may be
required. [s1] [s3]

Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Admission, enrollment, satisfactory progress and background check are required for assistantship
appointment; combined campus appointments max 0.50 FTE/20 hours weekly. International Statement of
Finances and certified evidence are required before admission letter/I-20 release; central estimate is $56,975
for 2027-28. Department warns GTA support may fall short of required financial sponsorship. [s1] [s3] [s7]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
YES: mathematics GTA form is mandatory for consideration; without it committee assumes no interest. Use the
working top-of-page TA-form link; the older FAQ PDF link redirects to department home. Confirm submission
method with GPO because paper form gives a postal return address and direct reference instructions. [s1] [s6]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
PGRF offers ≥$37,000 per year for three years ($15,000 Presidential + ≥$7,000 Dean’s + ≥$15,000 RA),
tuition waiver but excludes enrollment/student fees. Faculty/college nomination required; full-time study,
progress and professional development conditions. International-specific exclusion is not stated; confirm
eligibility. Departmental fellowships and occasional research grants also exist. [s1] [s8] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
$70 international, nonrefundable, payable by credit card; application is not processed until paid. Domestic fee
is $60. [s2] [s3]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Published categories: current Auburn graduate students, full-time Auburn employees, active-duty military with
confirming letter, or second application to approved dual program. Select qualifying exemption in portal
payment section and provide evidence. UChicago/F-1 alone is not a listed category. [s2] [s5]

Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Central international page explicitly gives 2027-28 cost and new TOEFL scale. Mathematics page mixes
updated GRE optional policy with older mandatory-GRE and English text. Three months versus 90 days differ
by two days for Fall 2027. Admission transcript and GTA reference delivery instructions also need
reconciliation. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6] [s10]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Ask GPO for exact Fall 2027 GTA deadline and stipend; current admission letter count/prompts; whether Slate
letters satisfy GTA form; current form delivery; provisional English waiver before UChicago graduation; funding
offer/commitment date and PGRF internal deadline. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s6] [s9]

International GTAs are eligible but must demonstrate speaking proficiency independently of admission: current
TOEFL speaking 4.5 (23 old), IELTS speaking 7, Duolingo speaking 130 or Auburn iTEP speaking 4.5.

required. [s1] [s3]

Admission, enrollment, satisfactory progress and background check are required for assistantship
appointment; combined campus appointments max 0.50 FTE/20 hours weekly. International Statement of
Finances and certified evidence are required before admission letter/I-20 release; central estimate is $56,975
for 2027-28. Department warns GTA support may fall short of required financial sponsorship. [s1] [s3] [s7]

Other funding routes [Standing rule]
PGRF offers ≥$37,000 per year for three years ($15,000 Presidential + ≥$7,000 Dean’s + ≥$15,000 RA),
tuition waiver but excludes enrollment/student fees. Faculty/college nomination required; full-time study,
progress and professional development conditions. International-specific exclusion is not stated; confirm
eligibility. Departmental fellowships and occasional research grants also exist. [s1] [s8] [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
$70 international, nonrefundable, payable by credit card; application is not processed until paid. Domestic fee
is $60. [s2] [s3]

confirming letter, or second application to approved dual program. Select qualifying exemption in portal
payment section and provide evidence. UChicago/F-1 alone is not a listed category. [s2] [s5]
